name: Orbital Leiomyoma

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of benign smooth muscle tumor in orbital tissue
Orbital MRI or CT showing well-circumscribed, homogenous mass without bone invasion
Positive immunohistochemical staining for smooth muscle actin (SMA) and desmin
Progressive painless orbital mass with proptosis or displacement of the globe

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with positive immunohistochemistry and compatible imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of malignant smooth muscle tumors and other orbital neoplasms.

common.symptomName: Diplopia (double vision) due to extraocular muscle displacement
searchTerms: double vision from eye muscle shift
eyes seeing double due to muscle displacement
blurred or doubled images from eye muscle problem

common.symptomName: Visual field defects secondary to mass effect
searchTerms: loss of side vision from pressure
blind spots due to mass effect

occasional.symptomName: Epiphora (excessive tearing) due to lacrimal gland compression
searchTerms: watery eyes due to lacrimal gland swelling

occasional.symptomName: Headache localized to the orbital region

rare.symptomName: Optic nerve compression leading to decreased visual acuity
searchTerms: blurred vision from optic nerve pressure
reduced eyesight due to nerve compression
vision loss from optic nerve squeezing

rare.symptomName: Inflammatory signs such as redness or warmth over the orbit
Secondary glaucoma due to orbital mass effect
searchTerms: high eye pressure from orbital swelling
glaucoma caused by eye socket mass

imaging: Orbital MRI showing well-defined, homogenous soft tissue mass without bone erosion
CT scan demonstrating non-invasive orbital mass with possible mild enhancement
other: Histopathology revealing spindle-shaped smooth muscle cells with low mitotic activity
Immunohistochemical positivity for smooth muscle actin (SMA) and desmin

distinguishingFeatures: Vascular lesion with characteristic enhancement on imaging
Histology shows vascular channels rather than smooth muscle proliferation
Histology shows Antoni A and B areas and S-100 positivity
Usually encapsulated and may cause nerve-related symptoms
Histology shows rhabdomyoblasts and high mitotic index

redFlags: Severe visual impairment or sudden vision loss
Signs of orbital inflammation or infection
references: Font RL, et al. Orbital leiomyoma: clinicopathologic study of 6 cases. Arch Ophthalmol. 1995.
